issues.description: The package is a code/document/identifier-list release, while the two supplied sample builders and helper consume many external author-prepared inputs and generated intermediates. The GVKEY workbook is an identifier list, not the analysis panel. Each missing or unverified input is listed as a requirement; no absent local file or license is inferred from catalog misses or timeout probes.

Known helper writers feed named intermediate readers: ccmq() writes ccmq.csv; restated() consumes it and writes restated.dta; treatment() and sec_accesses() define treat ym2.csv and secview month.csv; secvsup(), ret_volatility(), rpnews(), analyst_num(), disclosure_timeliness() and investigating_Blackburne2020() define further producer outputs. RP news filtering depends on the separate RP sources.csv label map and distinct entity-validity crosswalk. Additional firm-month tables may be produced in the opaque range. Full invocation order and those contracts remain unresolved; known generated outputs are not reclassified as raw requirements.

Credential/connection candidate regions in the helper and the firm-month lines 225-265 were withheld from the safe source view. Their function bodies, producers, dynamic reads and effect on the driver cannot be claimed absent. The package remains unchanged; exact source/data contract and order for these regions are unresolved.

The supplied code imports pandas_market_calendars and business_calendar; their distributions are not present in the metadata-only environment check. Author-compatible versions and an isolated future environment need confirmation before an authorized attempt.

macFunction.py defines separate Windows-style analysis and data roots, and the entry scripts use both. A consistent portable mapping is needed in a separate working copy before a future authorized run.

evidence.quote:
Regulatory Transparency and Regulators’ Effort: Evidence from Public Release of the
                                SEC’s Review Work
evidence.description: The author datasheet identifies the same paper title as the frozen package header.

evidence.quote:
We use Python 3 to merge data files from different sources. “GT_FirmMonth_Sample.py” creates
a firm-month data structure from the CCM firm-quarters and merges in SEC access variables
aggregated at the firm-month level to construct the firm-month sample. “GT_Filing_Sample.py”
creates a filing data panel and merges in SEC access variables aggregated at the 30-(60-) day
window following the filing date to construct the filing sample. We use Stata to conduct regression
analyses.
evidence.description: The author datasheet describes the two Python sample builders and downstream Stata regressions.

evidence.quote:
The process to create SEC review variables is described in Section 2 above. The Python scripts
used to process and merge the firm-month sample and the filing sample are attached as
“GT_FirmMonth_Sample.py” and “GT_Filing_Sample.py,” respectively. “macFunction.py”
defines global variables and functions. We additionally include lists of the firm (GVKEYs) used
in the main analyses in the Excel file “GT GVKEY List.xlsx.”

actions.description: Confirm the quarterly, link, daily-return and restatement inputs required for the supplied financial intermediates.
steps: Use the supplied ccmq() filters and construction contract to assess whether COMP.FUNDQ and CCMXPF, together with the separate historical CIK/GVKEY map, satisfy the generated intermediate. Treat ccmq.csv as generated; do not require byte identity to ccmq.dta when a compatible field-preserving route is supported.

Confirm genuinely unprobed fields (including fyq, SIC/state, issuer IDs and source-format flags as applicable) and pre/post-sample quarters needed for firm minimum-date and one-quarter lead/lag calculations.
Confirm the daily CRSP date range required by ret_volatility() and match its identifier/date/value fields to the readable DSF candidate.
Match the FEED39 candidate's company/date semantics and historical coverage to non_reliance_restatement_95_20.dta before using it to generate restated.dta.
validation: Before a separately authorized run, compare source columns, identifiers, date intervals, filters and required pre/post history against each consumer and helper transform.
Verify generated ccmq.csv and restated.dta have the exact columns and keys expected by both sample builders.

Confirm event-study inputs cover the helper's preceding/following event windows and the authors' full filing/sample periods.

review_notes: This is the integrated static assessment of the supplied sample-construction code. The work item, frozen schema/rules, inventory, bounded probes and safe-screened sources were used; no author module was imported, compiled or executed, no author credentials were used, and no study data were opened beyond the explicitly bounded metadata/one-row probes.

The GVKEY workbook was probed only as an identifier list, not treated as an analysis panel. Catalog candidates and successful one-row probes support local fields/readability only; complete history, population coverage and author-export compatibility remain distinct open checks. Both RavenPack probe timeouts are preserved and are not interpreted as absent data or licensing barriers.

Opaque candidate-bearing ranges remain withheld in the safe source artifacts. The assessment records their unresolved producer, output-contract and order effects without claiming they contain no producers. Known visible helper writes and consumer reads are mapped separately.

The supplied datasheet mentions Stata regressions downstream, but this assigned package variant contains no regression consumer/program or analysis panel. Stata is therefore not listed as required software for the assessed supplied-code workflow; the scope description states this limit explicitly.

During bounded preparation, the first safe-view helper failed because a candidate scan artifact had a different JSON shape than expected; its original helper and traceback/addendum captures are preserved, and a versioned helper generated the safe views. Two wrong-working-directory process starts and one read-only jq summary failure are also preserved with their corrections. No author or data process ran.

Narrow source-map/input-granularity correction: independently consumed audit, segment, accrual, comment-letter, event-study, CMSW/crosswalk and firm-month SEC tables now have separate requirements/routes/actions. RP sources.csv is separately required for the four publication labels explicitly selected by the helper; SOURCE IDs remain unverified. Known ccmq filters/formulas and row-based leads/lags are credited, while unprobed fields and time/history remain open. Time partitions remain one product, and known generated ccmq.csv, restated.dta, secview month.csv and treat ym2.csv remain producer outputs rather than raw requirements.

A finalizer validation attempt rejected a new source quote because it did not match the cached source lines. That failed attempt and its raw diagnostic are preserved. The corrected draft relies on the existing hash-bound safe helper inspection artifact at displayed lines 232-235 for the RP source-map contract and does not repeat the unsupported source quote.

One draft-only correction-helper attempt stopped before writing because its safe-view line-indexing code omitted the standard-library re import. The exact process failure is preserved in probes/stage_003b_helper_failure_001.json; the saved helper was corrected before this successful attempt.
